Note::at¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

std::string_view Note::at(std::int64_t linear) const

Borrow One Cell By Its Flat Position¶

at(linear) is the direct, allocation-free way to inspect one cell when its row-major position is already known. It ignores axis boundaries: a shape [2, 3] Note is read as positions 0..5, with the final coordinate changing fastest. Use at_indices() when the coordinate itself carries meaning, and cell() when the result must outlive every Note that shares the source storage.

The returned std::string_view refers to the cell’s exact stored bytes. It does not copy, append a terminator, validate UTF-8, or stop at an embedded zero byte. The view remains valid only while at least one owning Note or TextRef keeps that storage alive. Materialize std::string(view) before the last owner dies if independent lifetime is required.

linear must be in [0, numel()). Unlike take(), this scalar accessor does not normalize negative positions; -1 is an error, not the last cell. Undefined and zero-element Notes have no valid position. Access is constant-time and performs no allocation or byte traversal.

Example 1: Read A Matrix In Row-Major Order¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{
        "r0c0", "r0c1", "r0c2", "r1c0", "r1c1", "r1c2"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{2, 3});

std::cout << "at(0)=" << grid.at(0) << '\n'
          << "at(4)=" << grid.at(4) << '\n'
          << "at(5)=" << grid.at(5) << '\n';

Output¶

at(0)=r0c0
at(4)=r1c1
at(5)=r1c2

The shape remains [2, 3]; only the lookup interprets it as a flat sequence.

Example 2: A Scalar Still Has One Cell¶

const auto scalar = pluss::note::make("solo");
std::cout << scalar.at(0) << '\n';

Output¶

solo

A rank-zero Note has numel() == 1, so position zero is valid even though it has no axes.

Example 3: Embedded Zero Bytes Are Not Terminators¶

const std::array<std::byte, 3> raw{
    std::byte{'A'}, std::byte{0}, std::byte{'B'}};
const auto view = pluss::note::bytes(raw).at(0);

std::cout << "bytes=" << view.size()
          << " values=" << static_cast<int>(static_cast<unsigned char>(view[0]))
          << ',' << static_cast<int>(static_cast<unsigned char>(view[1]))
          << ',' << static_cast<int>(static_cast<unsigned char>(view[2])) << '\n';

Output¶

bytes=3 values=65,0,66

Use size() and byte-aware consumers rather than C-string functions for raw byte Notes.

Example 4: Copy A Borrow Before Storage Expires¶

std::string retained;
{
  const auto temporary = pluss::note::make({"alpha", "beta"});
  retained = std::string(temporary.at(1));
}
std::cout << retained << '\n';

Output¶

beta

For a zero-copy retained handle instead, assign temporary.cell(1) to a pluss::TextRef.

Example 5: Invalid Positions Reject¶

const auto values = pluss::note::make({"a", "b"});
auto rejected = [](std::int64_t index) {
  try { (void)pluss::note::make({"a", "b"}).at(index); }
  catch (const pluss::Error&) {
    std::cout << "at(" << index << "): rejected\n";
  }
};
rejected(-1);
rejected(2);

Output¶

at(-1): rejected
at(2): rejected
